critical_steps: For K e_n=e_n/n and f_n=g_n=n e_n, the transformed pair is exactly the standard orthonormal basis.
The transformed weaving energy is ||h||^2, hence it dominates ||K*h||^2 with universal K-frame bound one.
At x_N=e_N/N in R(K*), the original weaving energy is one while ||x_N||^2=1/N^2, so no uniform upper bound exists.
When K has closed range, the minimum-norm preimage h=(K*)^dagger x satisfies ||h||<=||K^dagger|| ||x||, supplying the missing upper estimate.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact diagonal-operator counterexample on l2 together with a Moore--Penrose proof of the closed-range repair.
integrity.unproved_limits: No weakest pair-dependent replacement for closed range is characterized.

scientific_limitations: The result refutes Proposition 2.5 for general bounded K and proves a sufficient closed-range repair.
Closed range is not asserted to be necessary for every fixed pair of sequences; pair-specific upper control can be weaker.
An unindexed note or informal correction may contain the same nonclosed-range observation.
title: Closed range repairs the image characterization of woven \(K\)-frames
